macro.summary: Renewed US-Iran fighting around the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent back above $90, lifted energy shares and long Treasury yields, and pressured broad US equities. The physical AI/power thesis remains intact, but the discount-rate hurdle for expensive long-duration equities has risen.
macro.oil: Brent settled around $90.49 and WTI around $85.76 after renewed attacks. The key persistence test is physical Hormuz flow rather than headlines alone; Gulf exports have partially recovered but remain disrupted.
macro.rates: The US 10-year yield rose toward the upper-4% area as inflation and September Fed-hike expectations increased after Jackson Hole.
macro.nextMacroCheckpoint: August ISM Manufacturing on 2026-09-01 at 10:00 ET; August ISM Services on 2026-09-03 at 10:00 ET.
macro.portfolioImplication: Prefer cash-generative energy, grid, water, cooling and operating nuclear. Raise entry hurdles for pre-profit nuclear, weak solar, expensive event-driven technology and other duration-heavy names.

holdingsMarketReview.read: Best fundamental anchor in the portfolio and tactically helped by the oil shock. Do not mechanically add into a war-premium spike; prefer a pullback or evidence that physical Hormuz disruption persists.
Fundamentals remain strong and relatively insulated from the oil/AI-capex cycle, but the share price is range-bound and organic growth needs to reaccelerate before this becomes a high-urgency add.
FY26 operating improvement is real, but rising global yields increase the penalty on leverage. Keep the upgraded fundamental view while avoiding a chase after the recent rerating.

The stock remains structurally exposed to Johor data centres and power scarcity, but heavy capex, leverage and AI-financing scrutiny make cash conversion the key next test. It was still up roughly 6.5% versus the 21 Aug close despite the latest pullback.

holdingsMarketReview.action: HOLD / OPPORTUNISTIC SMALL ADD ONLY AFTER STABILISATION
holdingsMarketReview.read: The selloff is driven by GTA VI leak anxiety plus a weaker macro tape. Rockstar still targets 19 Nov 2026 and BofA found no clear evidence of a distributable game copy. The cheaper price improves asymmetry, but do not average aggressively while leak-driven volatility is unresolved.

holdingsMarketReview.action: HOLD / CONSIDER TRIM INTO EVENT STRENGTH
holdingsMarketReview.read: Shares are rallying into the 3 Sep Cybercab event while the valuation remains extreme relative to current earnings and rates are rising. Avoid adding before the binary catalyst; require measurable deployment economics rather than another narrative reset.

This remains the weakest holding: price is at the 52-week low while Q2 revenue, profit and vessel utilisation deteriorated. Higher oil improves sentiment but does not repair work-order conversion. Treat a rebound as an opportunity to reassess position size rather than an invitation to average down.

upgrades.reason: Price returned to the original buy zone while structural backlog thesis remains intact.
Price cleared the prior $36–36.50 confirmation zone as oil risk premium returned.
FY26 revenue +61% and PAT +92% validate the Malaysia substation/grid thesis.

downgrades.reason: Higher oil/gasoline and rates worsen the consumer/financing backdrop.
Price fell ~7.8% from the prior snapshot toward invalidation while rates rose.
Price weakened further without resolving dilution or commercialisation risk.
A fresh 6%+ daily decline confirms fundamentals are still dominating technical support.

newOpportunityScreen.name: Ranhill Utilities Berhad
newOpportunityScreen.thesis: Direct Johor data-centre water bottleneck exposure through the state's source-to-tap operator. Research estimates planned data-centre investment could add roughly 700–800 MLD of water demand; Ranhill SAJ has a dedicated RM5.33/m3 data-centre tariff.
newOpportunityScreen.counterThesis: Electricity is a major operating cost, so the same energy-inflation regime that boosts XOM can squeeze Ranhill margins. This is a selective entry, not a one-way AI proxy.

newOpportunityScreen.name: Listed tanker operators
newOpportunityScreen.status: research queue — do not chase yet
newOpportunityScreen.thesis: Tanker freight rates are at historic highs as Hormuz restrictions reduce effective vessel capacity. This is a direct hard-asset/logistics expression of the conflict rather than another oil producer.
newOpportunityScreen.counterThesis: The trade can unwind violently if Strait traffic normalises; vessel values and freight equities have already rerated. Require company-level fleet, charter and valuation work before promotion.

newOpportunityScreen.name: CF Industries
newOpportunityScreen.thesis: Middle East conflict has disrupted fertilizer supply chains while El Nino and food-price pressure raise the value of secure domestic nitrogen production. CF is also building additional US capacity.
newOpportunityScreen.counterThesis: Natural-gas feedstock costs are rising and the stock has already benefited from the scarcity narrative. Need a margin/valuation screen before any buy call.

keyConclusions: Best fresh entry among existing US watchlist names: PWR, with MOD and XYL requiring support confirmation.
Best tactical energy change: HAL confirmation improved, but XOM remains the higher-quality owned exposure and CVX should not be chased above the old entry zone.
Best new structural adjacency: RANHILL for Johor water; MNHLDG for substations is promoted from research priority to actionable watch.
Weak-price traps remain ENPH, SMR and 0968.HK; cheaper is not the same as better.
TTWO's 6%+ selloff is more interesting than TSLA's 5%+ pre-event rally on risk/reward, but TTWO still needs leak-volatility stabilisation.
September 1 ISM Manufacturing is the next major macro test for the physical-stack thesis and rate/inflation mix.
